warrant: Each original text table is compared separately with abs(candidate-reference) <= atol[file] + 1e-4*abs(reference); the atols are scalCls=1e2, lensedCls/lensedtotCls/lenspotentialCls/totCls/scalarCovCls=1e-1, tensCls=1e-2, matterpower=1, and transfer_out=1e3. The reference split at atol is only for bulk/near-zero diagnostics, never a switch in the pass rule. config.f90:40 sets base_tol=1e-4 and, because every deck inherits transfer_high_precision=T, cmbmain.f90:1109-1111 tightens scalar transfer integration to 1e-6; six-significant-digit printing contributes a worst-case 1e-5 relative quantum and the measured x86-to-legacy floor on magnitude-carrying entries is 9.98e-6. The absolute terms sit ten print quanta above each file's peak quantum and cover catastrophic-cancellation entries such as scalarCovCls at 9.9e-32 and lenspotentialCls at 8.8e-48. Dropping dark-energy or EFT terms in equations.initial/derivs (equations.f90:1963-2306 and 2469-3689) changes transfer growth and the lensed and unlensed spectra beyond these bounds. Revision 5.6.0 says: "A heavy tail in a diagnostic array while the state arrays are clean is not a reason to abandon pointwise; give that array its own bound or exclude it as diagnostic, and say which in the warrant." The two base decks set get_vector_cls=F and get_tensor_cls=T, so all 73 numbered decks exercise tensor output but not vector initialv/derivsv/outputv; those routines remain owned without direct coverage. The upstream test_spectra.sh loops over parameters/*.ini (75 files including the two bases); this check reads its exact model list from models.txt, and the 11 disjoint manifests cover all 73 numbered decks. Determinism is claimed only for the repeated 2_PEFT_Omega_const_1.ini run, which reproduced eleven files byte-for-byte. Unowned paths are classified: halofit is excluded because do_nonlinear=0 in both bases; InitialPower is a shared dependency exercised by every check; the DarkEnergyInterface.f90 and DarkEnergyFluid.f90 scientific paths are shared dependencies of gr-baseline with EFTflag=0, while DarkEnergyPPF.f90 and DarkEnergyQuintessence.f90 alternatives are not exercised (parameter parsing may still occur in all runs); PowellMinimize belongs to the EFT models/background module.  The scalar integrator's local tolerance and the five-model print-floor observation do not prove global output accuracy for every deck; K-mimic sensitivity outside the graded window is now measured (see the kmimic check's own warrant). The fingerprint covers task contract files, not the skill version itself. On the 2026-09-06 x86 selfcheck the -O1 altbuild left this check's output at bound_fraction 1e-05 of the bound (no material movement); on this check the two-ulp variant (bound_fraction 0.0497, margin 20x) is the only calibration of the bound, and the altbuild floor calibrates nothing here. Per-column measurement (comment/measurements/per_column.md with its leaf-wide summary per_column_summary.md, 2026-09-06 x86 run2, nominal versus the two-ulp variant on all 12 checks, 248,527 angular rows) separates the columns the atol alone grades from the columns the rtol term holds on magnitude, and maps each atol-only column to the file where the same observable is graded on magnitude: unlensed scalar EE in scalCls (|r| <= 100 on all but 2 rows) is graded on magnitude in lensedCls, lensedtotCls, lenspotentialCls, totCls and scalarCovCls ExE at atol 0.1 (98.6 to 98.9% of rows above the atol); the lensing potential in lenspotentialCls PP and scalarCovCls PxP (|r| <= 2.4e-7) is graded on magnitude by scalCls PP on every row (|r| up to 1.0e7 against atol 100); the T-phi cross in lenspotentialCls TP and scalarCovCls TxP/PxT (|r| <= 0.27) is held on magnitude only by scalCls TP on the 4.4% of rows with |TP| > 100, at low ell; B-modes are held on magnitude only near their peaks, lensedCls/lensedtotCls BB on the 1.7% of rows above 0.1 and tensCls BB on the 8.5% of rows above 0.01, while totCls BB and lenspotentialCls BB (|r| <= 0.067) are atol-only; the E-phi cross (lenspotentialCls EP, scalarCovCls ExP/PxE, |r| <= 1.2e-3), the source-window pairs TxW2, ExW1, ExW2, PxW1, PxW2, W1xW2 and W2xW2 (|r| <= 7.2e-3; W1xW1 and TxW1 reach the atol on 1.2% and 0.3% of rows), and transfer_out Weyl (|r| <= 0.79) and v_b-v_c (|r| <= 287, atol 1000) are graded by the atol alone in every file that carries them, so they are effectively ungraded and are listed under blind spots in comment/README.md. The magnitude-carrying columns (TT, lensed EE, TE, scalCls PP, matterpower P, the transfer_out species and velocity columns) are held by the rtol term; on rows above the atol the measured relative error is at most 9.4e-6 on matterpower, 5.8e-6 on transfer_out and 9.75e-6 on tensCls, and TT and TE show larger relative errors (4.8e-5 and 2.1e-3) only on rows where the absolute term still supplies a comparable or larger share of the bound, consistent with the leaf-wide maximum bound fraction of 0.245 (K-mimic).
altbuild: run.sh altbuild builds the same pinned source with gfortran -O1 -w in place of the graded -O3 -w (fortran/Makefile FFLAGS), and the Horndeski coefficient C files (hdsk_coefficients.c, hdsk_coefficients_f.c) at -O1 without -ffast-math in place of the graded -O3 -ffast-math (fortran/eftcamb/eftcamb_build.make CFLAGS), same CLUSTER_SAFE=1 make camb target; gfortran -O0 was tried first and measured to SIGSEGV on this x86 host inside __results_MOD_cambdata_setparams even with an unlimited stack and OMP_STACKSIZE=512M (see comment/README.md), so -O1 is the smallest optimization-level change that runs. A correct candidate on a different compiler or optimization level could plausibly produce -O1-like floating-point contraction, evaluation order, and the absence of fast-math reassociation, so this is a legitimate alternative build to grade nominal against.
